name: Temporary Protection for Persons Displaced from Ukraine (Government Decision No. 21 of 18.01.2023)

qualifying_event.description: Group-based protection (not individual refugee status determination) for persons displaced from Ukraine due to the war, implementing an EU-aligned temporary protection framework via Government Decision No. 21 of 18.01.2023, extended by subsequent decisions to 1 March 2027. Beneficiaries must re-apply online between 1 February and 30 April 2026 for automatic extension.
qualifying_event.evidence_hint: Proof of displacement from Ukraine and of habitual residence there before the qualifying date.

requirements.blocker_text: Displaced from Ukraine due to the war and covered by Government Decision No. 21 of 18.01.2023 as extended.

evidence_required.document: Proof of displacement/habitual residence in Ukraine

outcome.duration_length: extended to 1 March 2027 as of this build; status lapses on voluntary repatriation or an absence of more than 45 cumulative days from Moldova
outcome.physical_presence_requirement: status lapses after more than 45 cumulative days' absence from Moldova

sources.title: Government of Moldova -- press release: temporary protection for persons displaced from Ukraine extended to 1 March 2027; beneficiaries must re-apply online 1 Feb-30 Apr 2026 for automatic extension

Refworld (UNHCR-hosted) -- Government Decision No. 21 of 18.01.2023 with 2025 amendments, English translation: legal residence, work authorization, education access, healthcare, social services; status lapses on voluntary repatriation or 45+ cumulative days' absence

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Moldova). STATUS: PUBLISHED -- tier-1 Government of Moldova press release sourced for the core hard requirement and the current extension date, corroborated by a tier-2 UNHCR-hosted text of the underlying decision. DISTINCT FROM md_international_protection.json: this is GROUP-BASED temporary protection under an EU-aligned framework, not individual Refugee Convention status determination -- no persecution test, no BMA eligibility interview, just proof of displacement from Ukraine. As a EU-candidate country bordering Ukraine, Moldova has hosted large numbers of Ukrainian displaced persons since 2022; this route reflects that specific, currently-active, time-bounded response rather than a permanent feature of Moldovan immigration law -- application_window fields reflect the stated 2026 re-registration window, and the whole route is understood to be time-limited/renewable-by-government-decision rather than a standing legal category. work_rights and study_rights set to 'full' per the source, notably generous compared to many asylum-seeker (as opposed to recognized-refugee) regimes elsewhere in this dataset.
